newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real up, mkt still awaits mini-band drop.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real up, mkt still awaits mini-band drop.

text.p: Brazil's real rose 0.03 percent to close at 1.0816 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market with continued expectations of a lowering in the reais-dollar mini-band, dealers said.
As the Central Bank did not decrease the mini-band Thursday, some banks decided to sell dollars, causing the real to rise, dealers added.
Despite selling dollars, players were still awaiting a drop in the mini-band, they said, noting that some people sold because it was too expensive to carry dollars over to Friday.
"The market definitely expects a mini-band decline on Friday since the Central Bank did not do anything Thursday," one trader at a large local bank said.
The current mini-band was set by the Central Bank on July 17 at between 1.0810 and 1.0860 reais per dollar and traders had been expecting a 0.1 percent decline Thursday.
So far this month, the mini-band has fallen 0.42 percent against the dollar compared to monthly declines of between 0.57 and 0.61 percent in the past six months.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real closed at 1.0874 per greenback, down 0.01 percent.
In the parallel market, the real rose 0.17 percent to end at 1.148 per dollar.
